Compare the locations of a connection with one of them

Source: R/inspect.R
store_status.Rd

For each location other than the source and each dataset, compares the catalogs held by the connection: a copy is the same when its version equals the source's. The source is the primary unless from names another location. No file is read and no location contacted; run store_refresh() first to compare what is stored now.

Usage

store_status(st, from = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'rcs_status'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

from

NULL (the default) to compare every secondary location with the primary, or the address of a location of the connection (as given to store_connect()) to compare every other location, the primary included, with that one.

x

The result of store_status().

...

Passed on to the tibble's print method.

Value

A tibble with one row per location other than the source and dataset of the source catalog (index tables included), plus one per dataset found only in that location, ordered by location (in connection order) and dataset:

  • dataset: the full name;

  • location: the address of the location compared with the source;

  • status: "same", "differs" (another version), "missing" (not in that location), "primary only" (not in that secondary location because the dataset is kept in the primary only, see store_write()'s locations), "extra" (only in that location), or "unavailable" when it or the source could not be reached;

  • newer: for "differs", the side with the later updated time, "source" or "target" (the location of the row); NA otherwise. A hint only: the clocks of the machines that wrote may differ;

  • primary_version, location_version: the versions compared; primary_version is the source's (the primary's by default);

  • primary_updated, location_updated: the times of the last writes, primary_updated in the source.

The attribute source holds the address of the source. Zero rows when the connection has no other location. store_sync() brings differing datasets up to date in the secondaries that hold them; store_sync(st, datasets = "<name>") or store_sync(st, all = TRUE) also copies missing ones (all = TRUE leaves out those kept in the primary only).

Details

Printed, the source is named first; the addresses of the other locations are listed once above the table and the column location shows their numbers, so that long addresses stay readable; the values of the column are the full addresses.

See also

store_datasets(), store_refresh(), store_sync().

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-status")
st <- store_connect(
  file.path(root, "primary"),
  secondary = file.path(root, "copy"),
  create = TRUE
)
store_write(st, rcs_sim_table(100, seed = 1), "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 100 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary    /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-status/primary  2/2
#>   files sent  23.8 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ secondary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-status/copy     2/2
#>   files sent  23.8 kB  0.1s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 2 locations. Catalogs updated.
store_status(st)
#> Source: /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-status/primary
#> Locations: [1] /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-status/copy
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   dataset     location status newer primary_version  location_version
#>   <chr>       <chr>    <chr>  <chr> <chr>            <chr>           
#> 1 sales/daily [1]      same   NA    0f9e01793cbea58a 0f9e01793cbea58a
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: primary_updated <dttm>, location_updated <dttm>
store_status(st, from = file.path(root, "copy"))
#> Source: /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-status/copy
#> Locations: [1] /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-status/primary
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   dataset     location status newer primary_version  location_version
#>   <chr>       <chr>    <chr>  <chr> <chr>            <chr>           
#> 1 sales/daily [1]      same   NA    0f9e01793cbea58a 0f9e01793cbea58a
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: primary_updated <dttm>, location_updated <dttm>
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
